# Reconstruction V3 contract (reviewed)

Root owns shared schema/API/provider and import integration. V3 replaces room-edge enclosure generation with an explicit physical-boundary description. Original-page coordinates, source-only QA, unknown scale and V2 portable imports remain compatible.

## Description

Keep BuildingDescription(floors, limitations) and existing floor source/order/orientation/calibration fields. RoomDescription adds environment indoor|outdoor|unknown; its polygon creates only an IfcSpace footprint, never walls. Add floor.boundaries, floor.features and floor.unresolved. No list caps.

BoundaryDescription: key:str (unique within floor), kind wall|railing|open_edge, label, segment:list[Point], source:PageRegion, thickness_segment:list[Point] (empty if unknown), basis observed|inferred, note. Physical wall records describe one shared wall axis spanning any explicitly hosted gaps; each shared physical boundary is listed once. Thin door leaves, arcs, furniture and annotations are not walls. Explicit railings/open edges never become full-height walls.

OpeningDescription replaces host_room/host_edge with host_wall:str|null (boundary key); retain kind, label, segment, source, basis, note. Segment endpoints identify the actual gap on the wall, not a drawn door leaf or swing arc. Unknown host stays null and yields an unresolved record, never arbitrary attachment. No valid host depends on a room polygon surviving.

FeatureDescription: kind stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other, label, polygon:list[Point], source:PageRegion, basis, note. Every meaningful depicted feature is included, with simple footprint symbols sufficient; no vertical dimension is required. Generic other+label covers features outside the named categories. UnresolvedDescription: label, category:str, source:PageRegion, reason. Use for ambiguous classification or unlocatable geometry; annotations are excluded. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual extents cannot be resolved.

## Scene and IFC

SceneElement adds representation reconstructed|schematic|unresolved, semantic_type:str, environment indoor|outdoor|unknown. Extend kind to room/outdoor/wall/railing/open_edge/door/window/stairs/furniture/fixture/other. Unresolved elements have geometry=None but retain stable GlobalId, source, label and note reason. Every described entry must appear as rendered/schematic/unresolved, including validation omissions. Stable namespace keys must not renumber after omission. No silent omission counter as the only record.

Generated spaces are thin plates. Explicit walls use depicted thickness where a valid original segment establishes it, otherwise labeled display width. Openings create actual IfcOpeningElement void/fill relationships; host geometry is checked in aspect-correct coordinates. Reject incompatible/overlapping host associations to unresolved records. Never close a room edge to create a host. Features may be flat schematic IFC solids/symbols; any thickness, height, tread motif or vertical offset is a display assumption. No engineering/step-count claims.

New artifacts use manifest version3/marker v3 and embed the exact BuildingDescription plus all original normalized PNGs and per-element metadata. Reader accepts version2 artifacts without silently reclassifying them as native IFC. Version3 validates new semantic/status fields against per-element Psets, actual IFC classes/storeys and source regions. Unresolved entries use geometry-less semantic entities; all-unresolved scenes are allowed but explicitly state that no 3D geometry was reconstructed; the original source and unresolved inventory remain available. Native IFC import unchanged.

## Comparison UI

Root provides Scene.comparison: list[PlanComparison] computed after actual IFC tessellation. Each entry: element_id, floor_id, page, layer spaces|walls|openings|features|unresolved, polygons:list[list[list[float]]], lines:list[list[list[float]]], method:str, cut_height:float|null. Coordinates are normalized ORIGINAL page. They are inverse-transformed from actual meshes using stored SceneFloor.transform, without viewer explosion offsets. Walls use a horizontal cross-section through the assumed opening height (explicitly labeled display section), other elements use actual footprint projection. Unresolved entries carry no fabricated paths; UI uses element.source.bbox as a visibly different unresolved marker. Recompute on reopening; do not trust stale saved overlay paths.

Frontend adds a comparison control in the original drawing view, layer toggles and overlay opacity. Original orientation remains unchanged. Separate floor/page filtering, source-linked semantic/status counts and unresolved feature list make missing/incorrect features reviewable. Mesh highlights and assumption controls remain independent. Image-answer association may include new valid feature kinds, but unresolved or unrenderable entries cannot receive invented 3D highlights. Original source citations remain available.

## Budget and acceptance

Existing upload/IFC safeguards remain; no new floor/room/feature caps. Larger explicit inventories may exceed the current reconstruction token/time budget; measure live and change reconstruction-only settings if required, after communicating the tradeoff. No changes to gate/answer budgets or automatic provider fallback.

Acceptance requires visual original-coordinate comparison of both unchanged11397 floors and1794, explicit audit of outdoor boundaries, physical shared walls, every clear opening, stairs and furnishing/fixture coverage, plus live source QA/highlights/refusal and portable reopening. Passing mesh validation alone is not fidelity evidence. Record residual unresolved features/omissions honestly.

## Review resolutions
Duplicate boundary keys never resolve by first/last wins: all conflicting records and dependent openings remain unresolved. Invalid item geometry never invents an exact source region: retain a valid explicit item region, otherwise use the valid floor region and label it unlocalized; invalid floor/page references fail. An empty mesh set is a source inventory result, not a successful 3D reconstruction. The frontend uses safe empty bounds and a clear no-geometry notice.

# Blueprint QA

Junction hackathon prototype: upload an IFC or floor-plan JPG/PNG/PDF, orbit a source-linked Three.js model, and ask questions with evidence or an explicit limitation. Supplied IFC geometry is extracted. Drawing reconstructions become downloadable, source-linked IFC; unknown scale is explicitly unscaled.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.12+ and curl. No Node, database or cloud setup.

```sh
bash scripts/bootstrap.sh
# Add GEMINI_API_KEY to .env.local using your editor; do not overwrite existing keys.
# Optional model overrides are listed in .env.example.
bash scripts/dev.sh
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Uploads, previews and IFC import/viewing work without a key. Credentials stay on the server. Questions send source images or extracted IFC records to the explicitly selected provider. Image reconstruction also requires that provider. Three.js is pinned locally; there is no rendering service or CDN dependency.

## Try the two demo flows

1. Upload `duplex_arc.ifc` from the dataset's `ifc_bench` folder. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom. Ask **How many windows are in this IFC model?** The complete source catalog contains 24 windows. They highlight while other elements fade to 10% opacity. Click a highlighted object or its evidence row to inspect its GlobalId, STEP reference and properties. Rooms mean IFC spaces (21 in this model).
2. Upload unchanged `colorful-1794.png` or `colorful-11397.png` from `assets/junction-dataset/data/cubicasa5k`. Click **Generate building model**. Gemini describes every explicitly depicted floor across all pages; deterministic Python/IfcOpenShell creates the IFC and local Three.js renders it. The upside-down, side-by-side diagrams in 11397 require no manual editing. Use the floor selector and separate-floor display; click an object to inspect its original page region. Ask a floor-specific room question, requesting its full room region. Only reliable source-region/name associations highlight. Actual ceiling height remains unknown unless the original source supplies it.

**Highlight answer** and **Show assumptions** are independent controls. A scene is cached once for all pages; asking questions only updates highlights. Download its generated IFC and upload it in a fresh session: stable object IDs, original source PNGs, assumptions and provenance travel with the file. Unmapped answers keep their source evidence and do not invent a 3D selection.

## Switch providers

Set one variable in `.env.local` and restart the server:

```dotenv
# Temporary development (OpenAI Responses API)
AI_PROVIDER=openai
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-6.1-sol
# OPENAI_API_KEY must already be set locally.
```

```dotenv
# Final sponsor demo (default if AI_PROVIDER is absent)
AI_PROVIDER=gemini
# GEMINI_API_KEY must be set locally and have access to both configured models.
```

There is no automatic fallback. The UI identifies the active pipeline. OpenAI uses the same image-capable model for one structured sufficiency judgment and answer generation; the gate returns `confidence: null`. This is a development substitute for Gemini Decisions, not an equivalent calibrated decision model. OpenAI does document a separate Decisions endpoint, but this temporary adapter deliberately avoids a second model/access dependency. The original-source requirement, one-crop retry, citations and calculation checks are shared. Both pipelines can be confidently wrong; evaluate them separately before the Gemini demo. A Codex app login is not used: this adapter uses `OPENAI_API_KEY` with the Responses API.

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py
bash scripts/test.sh
```

Optional browser checks (real local HTTP flow with a clearly injected test provider, no Google calls):

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-browser.txt
.venv/bin/python -m playwright install chromium
RUN_BROWSER_TESTS=1 bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_browser.py tests/test_browser_3d.py tests/test_browser_v2.py
# Optional actual-dataset import validation:
IFC_SAMPLE=/path/to/duplex_arc.ifc bash scripts/test.sh tests/test_ifc_import.py
```

Browser tests skip by default. They cover both 3D acceptance flows plus PDF/citation navigation, replacement, insufficient/unclear/error states, mobile layout, busy-state locking, and preview without credentials. The real IFC browser case requires the local duplex sample; provider calls in browser tests are explicitly injected fixtures.

The bootstrap creates a local `.venv` and installs pinned `requirements.txt`. On hosts lacking ensurepip, it bootstraps pip from the official PyPA endpoint. Never install into system Python. `requirements.in` records direct dependencies; regenerate the lock in a clean project environment after intentional dependency updates.

## Scope and behavior

Historical Gemini compatibility diagnosis is in [GEMINI_FIX.md](docs/GEMINI_FIX.md); current reconstruction verification is in [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_VERIFICATION.md](docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V2_VERIFICATION.md). Reconstruction uses medium thinking after a live comparison improved multi-floor footprint coverage; source answering and Decisions keep their existing settings. Array upper bounds are enforced locally rather than sent in Gemini's structured-output schema. Approximate geometry still must pass local validation. Invalid or ambiguously overlapping room footprints are omitted with a visible partial-model warning; if none remain, no model is saved. Source-based answers remain available.

- One document at a time: JPG/PNG or PDF up to 10 MiB and five pages. Oversized PDFs are rejected, not silently truncated.
- Uncompressed IFC STEP up to 25 MiB, 4,000 elements and one million triangles. GlobalIds and source units are preserved; world geometry is in metres. Geometry failures retain source records and count membership. Inspector properties are bounded to 48 primitive values per object; inference sees the first 12 with explicit omission warnings.
- For genuinely supplied IFC only, exact English whole-model count questions use deterministic catalog counts after the same sufficiency gate. Qualified/floor-specific questions use the normal gated source-answer path; no extra intent model. Counts describe the uploaded model, not physical-building completeness.
- The selected gate evaluates whether the inspected source supports the question: sufficient, insufficient or unclear. One additional inspection is allowed for unclear results.
- The selected model generates structured answers and source references. A sufficiency score does not prove the answer is correct. References are model-proposed regions for human verification.
- Missing scale/dimensions remain unknown. Assumptions are labeled proposals, never facts about the uploaded building. Similar-building retrieval is deferred.
- Drawing reconstruction covers explicitly depicted floors, room footprints, simple boundaries, and reliably hosted doors/windows. There are no extraction floor/room/vertex caps. Existing upload, IFC and provider budgets still apply. Unknown scale uses IFC `UNSCALED_DISPLAY_UNIT`, never metres; an explicitly cited physical dimension can calibrate footprints. Heights/thicknesses and missing vertical opening dimensions remain display assumptions. Unsupported alignment is schematic; vertical separation is only a viewer effect.
- Generated IFC is derived visualization, never authoritative evidence—even after reopening. It embeds original normalized source PNGs and a validated provenance manifest. QA inspects those originals; generated inventory, dimensions and assumed heights do not enter factual context. Invalid or contradictory recognizable generated metadata is rejected rather than reclassified as supplied IFC. This is consistency validation, not cryptographic authenticity.
- API/configuration errors are displayed as operational errors, never as evidence insufficiency. No hidden fixture mode or provider fallback.

This is a local hackathon app, not a production service. Bind to loopback. It has no authentication or durable database. Runtime files are ignored by Git. See the API contract for exact source handling and limits.

Uploads are normalized to PNG with a maximum 4096-pixel edge (input images over 40 megapixels are rejected). Each server session holds at most 20 documents in a temporary directory under `.runtime`; normal shutdown removes that session. Restarting clears the document index. Initial model views are resized to 1600 pixels; a targeted retry uses a crop from the stored higher-resolution page. Fine text can still be unreadable. Server arithmetic verifies the operation, not the model's interpretation of operands or units.

## For subsequent agents

Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [reconstruction plan](docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md), [reconstruction contract](docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md), [base API contract](docs/CONTRACT.md), and [handoff](docs/HANDOFF.md). Root owns contracts/environment/integration; backend and frontend owners work in separate paths; an independent reviewer checks reliability and scope. Tests use injected providers and are not a model-quality evaluation. DXF/SVG/DWG, photorealism, Blender/MCP and cloud/HPC rendering remain deferred.

## Model-quality experiment

Use the same document/question pairs for ordinary Gemini and the gated pipeline. Measure answer coverage, error among answered questions, unsupported answers, unnecessary abstention, latency and token usage. Include deliberately incomplete and ambiguous drawings, as well as sparse JPGs with answerable questions. Split by drawing/building rather than translations or file formats. Keep reference answers out of runtime context.

API references: [Decisions](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api), [models](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models). The Decisions SDK requires google-genai 3.2 or later; this environment pins the installed version. Model names are configurable because account access can differ.

OpenAI references: [structured outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), [model catalog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models), [native Decisions (not used by this temporary adapter)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions).

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DXF/SVG/DWG, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.

# V3: explicit boundaries, visible features and source comparison

Independently reviewed plan; review resolutions are in RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. Concrete shared fields are owned by root in `docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md`; that contract governs implementation. Preserve the existing original-drawing → Gemini description → deterministic IfcOpenShell → generated IFC → Three.js pipeline, portable source provenance, source-based QA, caching and stable selections. The user's new scope includes every meaningful depicted building/furnishing feature as reconstructed geometry, a labeled schematic, or an explicit unresolved source item. It does not mean reproducing every annotation or decorative line.

## Diagnosis grounded in the saved final artifacts

Inspected the unchanged original `colorful-11397.png`, `/tmp/junction-live-v2-final/colorful-11397.png.ifc`, its matching scene JSON and the saved viewer image. The final IFC and scene agree: two storeys, 11 spaces, 57 walls, one door, no windows, and no stairs/furnishing elements. Every scene element has a mesh. Two terrace/balcony spaces are represented as ordinary rooms with ten automatically generated perimeter walls. These are actual IFC modeling/description limitations, not missing viewer meshes.

The current generator turns every retained room polygon edge into a wall. Room polygons describe usable spaces, not a structural wall inventory: this invents enclosure on outdoor edges, can duplicate shared boundaries and can turn a mistaken door-leaf/arc-shaped room boundary into a wall. In the inspected final artifact the diagonal wall centerlines are on the exterior-space outlines; we have not established that this exact run traced a door leaf. The design nevertheless permits that failure and must stop deriving walls from room perimeters.

The schema cannot represent indoor/outdoor distinctions, independent boundaries, stairs, tables, cabinets or sanitary objects. The current prompt requests only selected openings, and opening hosts depend on retained room-edge indices; invalid/omitted room polygons can therefore remove otherwise visible openings. Some failed openings are summarized only as a count. The result cannot account for meaningful unrendered features individually.

The separate `/tmp/medium-quality-description.json` is another run: two floor records, 12 room records and four opening records. It is useful evidence of extraction coverage, but cannot explain individual omissions or geometry in the final IFC above. The saved final `1794` artifact has six spaces, 30 walls, five doors and two windows; use it as a regression baseline, not a ground-truth inventory.

## Narrow description changes (root finalizes contract)

Keep named x/y and left/top/right/bottom on the wire, original-page coordinates internally, existing floor regions/transforms/calibration/alignment/measurements, and medium reconstruction reasoning unless controlled live evidence warrants another choice. Extend each floor with the following compact records; no new arbitrary list caps.

- `rooms`: retain label/polygon/basis/note; add `environment: indoor|outdoor|unknown`. These produce footprint plates only. Unknown classification remains visible; it does not authorize enclosure. A terrace/balcony footprint is allowed without known elevation, floor thickness or railing height.
- `boundaries`: local stable `key`, `kind: wall|railing|open_edge`, label, original-page segment, source region, `thickness_segment` (empty if unknown), basis and concise note. One record per physical segment, shared by neighbouring spaces. Trace the depicted wall/railing itself; never door leaves, swing arcs, furniture edges or inferred room rectangles. Keep width/extrusion as current explicit display assumptions unless a valid thickness segment supplies depicted width. An open edge is recorded as open; it must not produce a wall.
- `openings`: retain door/window kind, label, original segment, source region and basis/note; replace `host_room/host_edge` with `host_wall: boundary key|null`. The host must be the correct same-floor explicit wall. Missing/ambiguous hosting is unresolved, not a guessed nearest wall. Unknown height/sill is compatible with a schematic opening and an explicit display assumption.
- `features`: `kind: stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other`, label, source region, polygon, basis and note. Source polygons may be approximate footprint symbols; unresolved geometry belongs in the unresolved list. Do not discard a visible object solely because its vertical dimensions are unknown. Stairs may be a low schematic footprint/tread indication; do not infer an actual rise, direction or connection between floors. Distinguish object geometry from the walls that surround it.
- `unresolved`: label, category, original source region and reason for visible but unclassifiable features or uncertain geometry. Server validation failures must produce equivalent persistent outcomes, not disappear into a warning count. Avoid duplicating the same item in feature and unresolved input lists. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual source extents cannot be resolved.

Keep extraction to the existing bounded request. Ask the model to account for the meaningful depicted categories across each entire floor, including openings and furnishings, without restricting it to a few illustrative examples. Model omissions are not automatically detectable: the inventory is a reconstruction audit aid, not a certified complete list or factual count source. Meaningful feature coverage needs a source-by-source visual acceptance pass.

## Deterministic generator behavior

1. Validate spaces, boundaries, openings and features independently. Invalid room polygons must not suppress valid explicit walls or openings. Existing room conflict rules remain within each floor; do not repair polygons or infer missing structural partitions.
2. Emit footprint plates for indoor/outdoor spaces with distinct provenance/classification and viewer styling. Emit IfcWall only from explicit wall records; emit railing geometry only from explicit railing records. Open edges remain visibly open. Shared boundary IDs map to one wall. Exact repeated/reversed copies can be recognized and reported; conflicting or uncertain duplicate interpretations remain unresolved rather than arbitrarily choosing one or silently merging nearby geometry. Duplicate/conflicting local boundary keys must never resolve by array order: mark the conflicting records and dependent openings unresolved unless identity is unambiguous.
3. Attach door/window void/fill relations only to their validated wall ID. Validate original endpoints/source bbox/floor consistency and the existing host-wall-band projection. Keep actual boolean openings in the IFC, rather than painting symbols on solid walls. If hosting fails, retain that exact opening as an unresolved inventory/source item. No automatic migration to a neighbouring wall and no widening source regions to force acceptance.
4. Generate simple, visibly differentiated feature geometry. Tables/cabinets may use IfcFurnishingElement, sanitary features an appropriate supported IFC product or generic furnishing subtype, and stairs a schematic product/footprint rather than a fabricated inter-storey connector. A small set of deterministic primitives is enough; this is not an asset library or detailed furniture modeling project. Record all display heights, thicknesses and other absent dimensions as assumptions.
5. Give every extracted/validated item a persistent compressed IFC GlobalId in its floor namespace. Persist its category, source, resolution status and reason. Unresolved entries become geometry-less semantic IFC entities with matching scene records; they have no invented mesh or location beyond their valid original source region. If malformed coordinates prevent reliable localization, use the known floor region explicitly marked coarse/unlocalized; do not manufacture a precise bounding box. Stable IDs survive validation omissions, caching and download/reopen. These inventories remain explicitly derived, never authoritative building counts.

Replace “at least one room must survive” with the reviewed contract's “at least one supported renderable element”: usable explicit walls/features may survive room interpretation failure. All-unresolved results remain explicit no-3D failures; do not claim a model was built. Root should retain the extraction/unresolved diagnostic payload for inspection when possible. This changes a current invariant and must be communicated; it is not a new feature-count limit.

## Scene, artifact and API additions

Root owns a versioned manifest/schema transition. New artifacts use version3/marker v3 and embed the exact BuildingDescription, so later diagnosis can connect an extraction to its actual exported artifact. Preserve existing v2 artifacts through an explicit reader branch; do not reinterpret their room-edge walls as new source-backed boundary descriptions. Current strict per-element Source/Assumptions/basis/note, actual IFC type/storey, original-page hash and classification checks remain.

Use the existing element list as the inventory: SceneElement adds `representation: reconstructed|schematic|unresolved`, `semantic_type`, `environment` and the existing note as a resolution reason. Kinds extend to room/outdoor/wall/railing/open_edge/door/window/stairs/furniture/fixture/other. This avoids forcing furniture into the old taxonomy or maintaining a redundant separate inventory. Keep unknown/partial coverage explicit. Reader checks stable IDs, actual IFC classes/storeys, source associations and all new status/semantic fields against per-element Psets. Unresolved entities are deliberately geometry-less entries in the generated catalog, not native source facts.

Add source geometry needed for meaningful comparison to manifest provenance where useful, but never use the provider's description as proof that rendered IFC matches it. All source images and per-floor transforms continue to survive download/reopen. Generated inventories, feature classes and dimensions are association hints only; the original-source QA gate and actual-height refusal remain unchanged. Extend validated highlight types only with appropriate source evidence; unresolved items open source evidence without fabricated mesh selections.

Retain the scene/download endpoints and cached model behavior. Root adds computed `Scene.comparison: PlanComparison[]`, with element_id/floor_id/page/layer, original-coordinate polygons/lines, method and optional cut_height. Compute after tessellation and recompute on reopening; never trust stale persisted comparison paths. Do not add an extra inference call or rebuild IFC for each overlay/selection. Source-overlay visibility remains separate from answer highlighting and assumptions controls.

## Source overlay must compare the actual IFC

Root's `app/comparison.py` computes the comparison from tessellated generated IFC meshes (and actual hosted void/fill geometry when needed), transformed back through the inverse stored floor matrix to the original page. The frontend places those vectors on the unchanged source image with separate layers for boundaries, indoor/outdoor footprints, openings, schematic features and unresolved regions. The overlay must not simply redraw the model's intended polygons or bounding boxes and call that a geometry check.

A full-height wall footprint projection hides opening cuts because the lintel above an opening projects over the gap. Either use appropriate mesh cross-sections or explicitly overlay actual IFC opening/fill footprints alongside projected wall footprints, with a clear legend. Do not claim that an uncut projection proves opening correctness. Compare multiple original floor regions on the same image without applying viewer explosion or display rotation to the source. Native source clicks, floor filtering and restored embedded pages must continue to work.

The UI should make unresolved items inspectable individually: selecting one shows its original region and reason. Show concise category/status totals for navigation, labeled as reconstruction inventory, not building facts. The user can inspect broad coverage without reading a long warning paragraph or searching only a selected set of doors.

## Design constraints to explain before implementation

- Independent explicit wall extraction replaces a wrong inference, but adds description content. The current token budget may then be exhausted; token-limit/provider failures remain operational errors. Run both live originals early. If a split extraction or budget change becomes necessary, root must explain that new call/budget tradeoff before implementing it; do not silently truncate furnishings/openings or add sample-count caps.
- Missing physical heights do not block schematic reconstruction. Assumptions remain visible and cannot answer factual height questions. Unknown scale, orientation, registration and inter-floor elevations retain current semantics.
- Source/host/geometry checks can leave clearly visible features unresolved. They must remain in the portable inventory and overlay, with reasons. This may still block visual acceptance if major recognizable features are absent; a successful HTTP status alone is not success.
- Existing upload, IFC byte/element/triangle and response safeguards remain. Additional source-linked features increase artifact size; oversized artifacts fail explicitly rather than silently dropping features/pages.
- Schematic feature silhouettes are sufficient for this hackathon. No new file formats, hidden-floor inference, structural completeness, parametric CAD editing, photorealism, cloud rendering or extra agent runtime.

## Ownership and sequence

1. **Root** finalizes reviewed schemas/inventory/status semantics, request budgets, provider prompt, v2/v3 artifact compatibility, reader/type checks, source QA/highlights, comparison computation and API integration. Root owns all live calls and the unchanged-original source comparison.
2. **Generator implementer** owns `app/ifc_generate.py` and `tests/test_ifc_generate.py` after approval: explicit shared boundaries, host-wall openings, indoor/outdoor footprints, feature primitives, unresolved outcomes, stable IDs and portable provenance. No provider/UI/reader changes without a separate assignment.
3. **Frontend implementer** owns agreed static viewer/UI paths: source overlay controls/legend, element-status inventory selection, distinct outdoor/feature rendering, preserved floor filters, independent assumptions and answer selections. Root supplies actual comparison vectors and the element-status contract first.
4. **Independent reviewer** reviews plan/contracts, then checks actual IFC/source agreement and changed provenance paths. The implementer does not serve as independent reviewer of this work. Root integrates and stops only after acceptance evidence and no unresolved blocking findings.

## Acceptance

- Unchanged original 11397 displays both depicted floors without manual cropping/rotation. Its terrace/balcony do not acquire enclosure merely from their footprint. Door leaves/arcs are not walls; shared physical boundaries are not doubled because two rooms reference them.
- Clearly depicted doors/windows are hosted on the right explicit boundary and affect actual IFC wall geometry. Uncertain ones remain source-linked unresolved items. Stairs and visible tables/cabinets/sanitary features are recognizable schematics or explicit individual unresolved items; do not omit them simply because height is unknown.
- Actual-IFC overlays on both original 11397 and 1794 make major boundary, opening and feature mismatches visible. Perform a meaningful-feature visual checklist for both images; report any uncovered categories/items honestly. Do not substitute the separate medium-description run for final artifact evidence.
- Focused tests cover independent room/wall survival, one shared wall, no outdoor automatic enclosure, non-wall door-swing feature, correct/invalid host IDs, source-region preservation, unresolved persistence, feature assumed heights, actual mesh inverse transforms and void overlays, plus v2/v3 export/reopen compatibility and reader validation.
- Live Gemini completes both unchanged originals within the explicitly agreed limits. Existing native IFC, QA, actual-height refusal, caching, highlighting/fading, floor source clicks and separate assumption controls pass. Export/reopen retains geometry, exact original pixels, inventory statuses and assumptions. Any unresolved visual blocker is reported rather than hidden behind partial-model warnings.
"""Only source properties enter answering. Inferred geometry is never evidence."""
import json
from collections import Counter

IFC_CONTEXT_PROPERTIES = 12


def source_context(document):
    scene = document.scene
    if not scene:
        return ""
    if document.kind == "ifc" and not scene.derived:
        # Every ID/class is included; properties are an explicitly bounded view.
        records = []
        omitted = 0
        for e in scene.elements:
            props = e.properties[:IFC_CONTEXT_PROPERTIES]
            omitted += len(e.properties) - len(props)
            records.append({"element_id": e.id, "ifc_type": e.ifc_type, "kind": e.kind,
                            "name": e.name, "storey_id": e.storey_id,
                            "source_step_id": e.source.step_id,
                            "properties": [p.model_dump() for p in props],
                            "omitted_properties": max(0, len(e.properties) - len(props))})
        context = {"source": "Extracted records from the uploaded IFC; not a claim about the as-built building",
                   "catalog_complete": scene.catalog_complete,
                   "counts_by_kind": dict(Counter(e.kind for e in scene.elements)),
                   "property_view": "At most 12 properties per element; other properties may exist in the IFC/inspector. Missing here does not establish absence from the original file.",
                   "omitted_properties": omitted, "warnings": scene.warnings, "elements": records}
        return json.dumps(context, ensure_ascii=False)
    # This is only a candidate association index. NO sizes/heights/properties/assumptions.
    return json.dumps({"association_index_only": "These are fallible image interpretations, NOT new source evidence. Answer from original pages. Use an ID only if its room label/region actually supports the answer; otherwise leave highlight_ids empty.",
                       "floors": [{"id":f.id,"label":f.label,"page":f.source.page,"bbox":f.source.bbox}
                                  for f in scene.floors],
                       "objects": [{"id": e.id, "kind": e.kind, "name": e.name,
                                    "page": e.source.page, "bbox": e.source.bbox, "floor_id":e.storey_id}
                                   for e in scene.elements if e.geometry is not None and e.representation != "unresolved"]}, ensure_ascii=False)
"""Conservative source-based associations. Never match by inferred geometry."""
import re


def iou(a, b):
    overlap = max(0, min(a[2], b[2]) - max(a[0], b[0])) * max(0, min(a[3], b[3]) - max(a[1], b[1]))
    union = (a[2]-a[0])*(a[3]-a[1]) + (b[2]-b[0])*(b[3]-b[1]) - overlap
    return overlap / union if union else 0


def validated_highlights(draft, document):
    scene = document.scene
    if not scene or draft.status != "answered":
        return []
    elements = {e.id: e for e in scene.elements}
    if document.kind == "ifc" and not scene.derived:
        backed = {e.element_id for e in draft.model_evidence}
        return list(dict.fromkeys(x for x in draft.highlight_ids if x in elements and x in backed))
    accepted = []
    for evidence in draft.evidence:
        box = evidence.bbox
        if (box[2]-box[0])*(box[3]-box[1]) >= .8:
            continue
        matches = [e for e in scene.elements if e.geometry is not None and e.representation != "unresolved" and e.source.page == evidence.page
                   and iou(e.source.bbox, box) >= .5]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            continue
        match = matches[0]
        text = " ".join(re.findall(r"\w+", (evidence.label + " " + evidence.observation).casefold()))
        name = " ".join(re.findall(r"\w+", match.name.casefold()))
        named = bool(name) and f" {name} " in f" {text} "
        if named and match.id in draft.highlight_ids:
            accepted.append(match.id)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(accepted))


def whole_model_count_kind(question):
    """Only unqualified, explicitly scoped counts. No fuzzy qualifier stripping."""
    match = re.fullmatch(r"how many (windows|doors|walls|rooms|spaces) (?:are |are there )?(?:in|does) (?:this|the|the uploaded) (?:ifc )?model(?: have)?\??", question.strip().lower())
    return {"windows": "window", "doors": "door", "walls": "wall", "rooms": "room", "spaces": "room"}.get(match[1]) if match else None

# API contract v1

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('docs/HANDOFF.md')
p.write_text('''# Agent handoff — 2026-11-14, reconstruction V3

## Status

V3 implements explicit physical boundaries, real wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, persistent unresolved records and an original-page comparison of actual reopened IFC geometry. **Full visual fidelity acceptance is not yet met.** Live source comparisons still find omitted/misplaced features; do not confuse passing API, IFC or browser checks with complete reconstruction.

Read [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md), [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md). V2 verification is historical. No commits, pushes, deployment, new dependencies or services.

## Run and inspect

Run `bash scripts/dev.sh`; open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Upload unchanged `assets/junction-dataset/data/cubicasa5k/colorful-11397.png` or `colorful-1794.png`, then Generate building model. In Drawing view enable Source comparison and toggle spaces/walls/openings/features/unresolved layers. These paths come from actual tessellated IFC meshes, inverse-transformed into the original page, not copied model description polygons. Walls use a section through assumed opening heights; other objects use footprint projection. Inspect missing features, incorrect enclosure and misplaced openings against the original.

The inventory links all interpreted entries to source evidence and exposes unresolved reasons. It does not certify complete coverage. Model view keeps orbit, floor filters, schematic separation, answer highlighting, 10% surrounding opacity, independent assumptions and source clicks. Download/reupload preserves source pages, exact V3 input description, stable IDs, statuses and assumptions. V2 artifacts still reopen.

## Provider configuration

Gemini is the default/final demo provider. Reconstruction alone makes one high-thinking `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` request; override explicitly with `GEMINI_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL`. Its 150-second timeout and 32,768-output-token budget are design choices measured against the richer inventory; large drawings can still exceed them. Truncated output is an operational error and cannot be cached. There is no automatic fallback or refinement stage.

`GEMINI_MODEL` remains the source-answer model (locally `gemini-flash-latest`); native Decisions, answer/crop budgets and refusal flow are unchanged. `.env.local` and credentials were not edited. `AI_PROVIDER=openai` remains an explicit temporary adapter with equivalent description fields and reconstruction-only time/token budgets. OpenAI V3 is SDK/regression tested, not live-fidelity verified. Health reports the reconstruction model separately.

## Geometry and provenance rules

- Room polygons make floor plates only. Explicit walls/shared boundaries are independent of rooms; invalid rooms cannot suppress valid walls/openings/features. Door leaves, swing arcs and furnishing outlines never automatically create walls.
- Door/window records name an explicit same-floor wall key. Valid gaps create actual IFC void/fill relationships. Invalid/ambiguous hosts stay unresolved, retaining source, stable ID and reason; no nearest-wall attachment.
- Outdoor space footprints do not imply enclosure. Open-edge polylines make flat markers; railings require explicit depicted support. No inferred hidden floors.
- Stairs/furniture/fixtures may be flat schematics when vertical shape is unknown. Stair marks are level symbols, not measured treads/rise or travel direction. Empty feature polygons request an explicit bbox schematic; malformed supplied geometry stays unresolved.
- V3 source boxes may provide context beyond the approximate floor bbox if the same-page regions overlap. Geometry anchors must remain in both floor and source region. Wrong-page/disjoint sources do not acquire invented geometry. V2 keeps its former containment validation.
- Unknown scale is `UNSCALED_DISPLAY_UNIT`, never measured metres. Supported calibration affects plan scale only. All missing vertical dimensions, opening heights/sills, symbol thicknesses and layout offsets remain assumptions.
- Generated IFC always reopens as derived drawing visualization, never as a factual native IFC catalog. Original embedded PNGs are validated by hash/dimensions; manifest, IFC properties, classes and storeys must agree. Original source QA excludes generated properties, geometry and assumed heights. The object index is only a fallible association aid. Unknown/ambiguous source associations retain citations without highlights.
- Every described item survives as reconstructed/schematic/unresolved. The model can still omit a source item completely: a valid inventory does not prove “everything shown” was found. All-unresolved scenes clearly report no 3D geometry and keep source inspection available.

## Verification and known blockers

The final live report and actual IFC/source overlays are recorded in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md). Temporary artifacts/scripts are under `/tmp/junction-v3/`; `/final/` denotes the final production-path run, `/pro/` an earlier controlled model comparison. Do not mix their descriptions or screenshots. No reference answer files were used.

- 194 backend/native-IFC tests passed; all 11 optional Chromium checks passed separately. Doctor passes. Native sample: `assets/junction-dataset/data/ifc_bench/duplex_arc.ifc`.
- Regression coverage includes room/wall independence, outdoor non-enclosure, true hosted gaps, duplicate/conflicting hosts, semantic feature classes, unresolved persistence, V2/V3 provenance and fresh-store reopening, source-only QA, conservative highlights and independent assumptions. A test moves actual IFC placement while holding provenance fixed and confirms the comparison moves.
- Independent read-only code review passed 106 focused checks with no code blockers. Independent visual review remains open because real extraction results still have fidelity blockers.
- Final1794 removes the earlier invented bedroom window, but still has a wall through the balcony, unresolved clear living-room/entry gaps, excessive thickness at the kitchen/bath partition and sink/hob misclassification. The earlier11397 Pro output missed a long interior partition/storage doorway and shortened/shifted some glazing. Final11397 findings are in the diagnosis report.

Do not claim full acceptance until original-coordinate review verifies those behaviors. Avoid hand-correcting acceptance fixtures and calling them live inference. Generic second-pass and upright-view experiments were tested but not adopted: they did not establish a reliable fidelity improvement.

## Workflow and limits

Root owns architecture/contracts/provider/reader/integration; backend planner/implementer owns IFC generation and generator tests; frontend owns UI/browser tests; independent reviewer stays read-only. Continue the AGENTS.md planning/review workflow and communicate any new design constraint before implementing it. No new extraction floor/room/vertex caps were added.

Existing drawing limits: 10 MiB, five pages, 40 MP input, 4096-pixel normalized edge; initial provider images use a 1600-pixel edge. IFC limits: 25 MiB, 4,000 elements, one million triangles; embedded original pages count toward artifact size. Native IFC properties retain 48-value inspector/12-value inference limits with warnings. Session cache is temporary; portable IFC download is the explicit persistence mechanism.

Defer photorealism, detailed stairs/roofs, structural engineering, new formats, Blender/cloud rendering, auth/database and reference-building retrieval. Multi-page/supported calibration flows are regression-tested; new live fidelity evidence uses the two PNG originals. Dataset ground-truth answers stay evaluation-only and were never runtime input.

The native duplex sample license attributes Duplex Apartment - arc to BSI (2020), buildingSMART International, CC-BY-ND-3.0. Dataset/source notes remain in 3D_PLAN.md and supplied license files.
''')

                                           UnitType="LENGTHUNIT",Name=DISPLAY_UNIT)
        self.project = self.model.create_entity("IfcProject",GlobalId=self.guid("project"),Name="Drawing-derived visualization",
            Description=ARTIFACT_MARKER,RepresentationContexts=[self.context],UnitsInContext=self.model.create_entity("IfcUnitAssignment",Units=[unit]))
        self.building = self.model.create_entity("IfcBuilding",GlobalId=self.guid("building"),Name="Depicted building",
            ObjectPlacement=self.placement,CompositionType="ELEMENT")
        self.aggregate(self.project,[self.building],"building")

    def guid(self, key):
        return ifcopenshell.guid.compress(uuid.uuid5(self.namespace,key).hex)

    def point(self, coordinates):
        return self.model.create_entity("IfcCartesianPoint",Coordinates=[float(v) for v in coordinates])

    def aggregate(self, parent, children, key):
        self.model.create_entity("IfcRelAggregates",GlobalId=self.guid("aggregate:"+key),RelatingObject=parent,RelatedObjects=children)

    def pset(self, entity, name, values, key):
        props = [self.model.create_entity("IfcPropertySingleValue",Name=k,NominalValue=self.model.create_entity("IfcText",v)) for k,v in values.items()]
        pset = self.model.create_entity("IfcPropertySet",GlobalId=self.guid("pset:"+key),Name=name,HasProperties=props)
        self.model.create_entity("IfcRelDefinesByProperties",GlobalId=self.guid("property:"+key),RelatedObjects=[entity],RelatingPropertyDefinition=pset)

    def solid_item(self, points, z, height):
        curve = self.model.create_entity("IfcPolyline",Points=[self.point(p) for p in points+[points[0]]])
        profile = self.model.create_entity("IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef",ProfileType="AREA",OuterCurve=curve)
        position = self.model.create_entity("IfcAxis2Placement3D",Location=self.point([0,0,z]))
        return self.model.create_entity("IfcExtrudedAreaSolid",SweptArea=profile,Position=position,
            ExtrudedDirection=self.model.create_entity("IfcDirection",DirectionRatios=[0.,0.,1.]),Depth=float(height))

    def solid(self, points, z, height):
        solid = self.solid_item(points,z,height)
        shape = self.model.create_entity("IfcShapeRepresentation",ContextOfItems=self.context,RepresentationIdentifier="Body",
                                         RepresentationType="SweptSolid",Items=[solid])
        return self.model.create_entity("IfcProductDefinitionShape",Representations=[shape])

    def stair_symbol(self, entity, points, z, thickness):
        """Flat, level graphic marks: no arrow, ascent, tread count or stair rise claim."""
        footprint=Polygon(points)
        left,bottom,right,top=footprint.bounds
        vertical=top-bottom >= right-left
        span=top-bottom if vertical else right-left
        band=span*.025
        items=list(entity.Representation.Representations[0].Items)
        # These are graphic positions, never a limit on extracted features or source steps.
        for fraction in (.2,.4,.6,.8):
            position=(bottom if vertical else left)+span*fraction
            strip=box(left,position-band/2,right,position+band/2) if vertical else box(position-band/2,bottom,position+band/2,top)
            clipped=footprint.intersection(strip)
            pieces=[clipped] if clipped.geom_type=="Polygon" else list(getattr(clipped,"geoms",[]))
            for piece in pieces:
                if piece.geom_type=="Polygon" and piece.area>0:
                    items.append(self.solid_item(list(map(list,list(piece.exterior.coords)[:-1])),z,thickness))
        entity.Representation.Representations[0].Items=items

    def product(self, ifc_type, key, name, polygon, z, height, storey, source, assumptions, basis="observed", note="", kind=None,
                representation="reconstructed", semantic_type="", environment="unknown"):
        if len(self.elements) >= MAX_ELEMENTS:
            raise DocumentError(f"Generated IFC exceeds the {MAX_ELEMENTS:,}-element limit; no inventory was truncated.",413)
        entity = self.model.create_entity(ifc_type,GlobalId=self.guid(key),Name=name,ObjectPlacement=self.placement,
                                          Representation=self.solid(polygon,z,height) if polygon else None)
        self.products.append(entity)
        scene = SceneElement(id=entity.GlobalId,kind=kind or {"IfcSpace":"room","IfcWall":"wall","IfcDoor":"door","IfcWindow":"window"}[ifc_type],
            name=name,ifc_type=ifc_type,storey_id=storey.GlobalId,source=source,assumptions=assumptions,
            geometry_origin="inferred",geometry=None,evidence_basis=basis,note=note,
            representation=representation,semantic_type=semantic_type or kind or ifc_type,environment=environment)
        self.elements.append(scene)
        self.pset(entity,PSET_NAME,{"Source":source.model_dump_json(),"Assumptions":json.dumps([a.model_dump() for a in assumptions]),
                  "EvidenceBasis":basis,"Note":note,"ArtifactMarker":ARTIFACT_MARKER,
                  "Representation":representation,"SemanticType":scene.semantic_type,"Environment":environment},key)
        return entity


def _rectangle(start, end, thickness):
    dx,dy = end[0]-start[0],end[1]-start[1]
    length = math.hypot(dx,dy)
    nx,ny = -dy/length*thickness/2,dx/length*thickness/2
    return [[start[0]+nx,start[1]+ny],[end[0]+nx,end[1]+ny],[end[0]-nx,end[1]-ny],[start[0]-nx,start[1]-ny]]


def _assumption(prop, value, unit, reason):

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DXF/SVG/DWG, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.

def reconstruct_scene(document, page_number, provider):
    """The legacy page argument does not restrict all-source floor extraction."""

class ProviderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, status: int = 502):
        self.message, self.status = message, status


def gemini_wire_schema(schema: dict) -> dict:
    """Relax array upper bounds only on Gemini's wire; validate the full model locally.

    The current endpoint rejects these bounds for our reconstruction schema. Walk
    schema locations, not arbitrary JSON values: a property named ``maxItems``
    or an object inside a default/enum remains ordinary data.
    """
    result = deepcopy(schema)

    def visit(node):
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            return
        kind = node.get("type")
        if kind == "array" or isinstance(kind, list) and "array" in kind:
            node.pop("maxItems", None)
        for keyword in ("$defs", "definitions", "properties", "patternProperties", "dependentSchemas"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, {}).values():
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("anyOf", "allOf", "oneOf", "prefixItems"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, []):
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("items", "additionalProperties", "contains", "not", "if", "then", "else",
                        "propertyNames", "unevaluatedProperties", "unevaluatedItems"):
            visit(node.get(keyword))

    visit(result)
    return result

def image_bytes(image, edge=1600):
    image = image.copy()
    image.thumbnail((edge, edge))
    output = BytesIO()
    image.save(output, format="PNG")
    image.close()
    return output.getvalue()


def views(document: Document, crop: CropRequest | None = None):
    """All source pages, plus at most one true crop from stored source pixels."""
    result = []
    for page in document.pages:
        with page.image() as image:
            result.append((f"Original source page {page.number}. Coordinates refer to this whole page.", image_bytes(image)))
    if crop:
        page = document.pages[crop.page - 1]
        with page.image() as image:
            left, top, right, bottom = crop.bbox
            region = image.crop((int(left * image.width), int(top * image.height),
                                 max(int(right * image.width), int(left * image.width) + 1),
                                 max(int(bottom * image.height), int(top * image.height) + 1)))
            try:
                result.append((f"Detail crop of original page {crop.page}, normalized bounds {list(crop.bbox)}. "
                               "This is the SAME source, not a separate object or page. Cite original-page coordinates.",
                               image_bytes(region, edge=2400)))
            finally:
                region.close()
    return result

class GeminiProvider:
    def __init__(self):
        config = settings("gemini")
        if not config["api_key"]:
            raise ProviderError("Gemini is not configured. Set GEMINI_API_KEY in .env.local and restart the server.", 503)
        self.model = config["model"]
        self.reconstruction_model = config["reconstruction_model"]
        self.decision_model = config["decision_model"]
        self.client = genai.Client(api_key=config["api_key"], http_options={
            "api_version": "v1beta", "timeout": 45000,
            "retry_options": {"attempts": 1},
        })
        self.usage = Usage()

    def close(self):
        self.client.close()

    def _decision_input(self, document, question, crop):
        contents = [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps({"question": question, "inspected_pages": [p.number for p in document.pages]})}]
        if context := source_context(document):
            contents.append({"type": "text", "text": context})
        for label, png in views(document, crop):
            contents.extend([{"type": "text", "text": label},
                             {"type": "image", "mime_type": "image/png", "data": base64.b64encode(png).decode()}])
        return contents

    def gate(self, document, question, crop=None):
        response = self.client.decisions.create(
            model=self.decision_model,
            input=self._decision_input(document, question, crop),
            questions={"sufficiency": {
                "type": "choice", "instructions": GATE_INSTRUCTIONS,
                "criteria": {
                    "sufficient": "Essential evidence is present and interpretable; direct answers or supported calculations are possible without invented facts.",
                    "insufficient": "Essential information is absent from the inspected material, so the question cannot be answered from it.",
                    "unclear": "Legibility, ambiguity, contradictory evidence or uncertain scope/completeness prevents a determination; inspect further or clarify.",
                },
            }},
        )
        answer = response.answers["sufficiency"]
        usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
        self.usage.input_tokens += getattr(usage, "total_input_tokens", 0) or 0
        self.usage.output_tokens += getattr(usage, "total_output_tokens", 0) or 0
        return GateResult(decision=answer.choice, confidence=answer.confidence)

    def _generate(self, document, question, instruction, schema, crop=None, *, thinking_level=None, timeout_ms=None, max_tokens=8192, model=None):
        parts = [types.Part.from_text(text=json.dumps({"question": question}))]
        if context := source_context(document):
            parts.append(types.Part.from_text(text=context))
        for label, png in views(document, crop):
            parts.extend([types.Part.from_text(text=label), types.Part.from_bytes(data=png, mime_type="image/png")])
        response = self.client.models.generate_content(
            model=model or self.model, contents=parts,
            config=types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=instruction, temperature=0,
                                               response_mime_type="application/json", response_json_schema=gemini_wire_schema(schema.model_json_schema()),
                                               max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
                                               http_options=types.HttpOptions(timeout=timeout_ms) if timeout_ms else None,
                                               thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=thinking_level) if thinking_level is not None else None),
        )
        usage = response.usage_metadata
        self.usage.input_tokens += getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0

from typing import Annotated, Literal
from pydantic import BeforeValidator, WithJsonSchema, model_validator
from .schemas import StrictModel


def _named_coordinates(value, names):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if set(value) != set(names):
            raise ValueError("Coordinate object has unexpected fields")
        return [value[name] for name in names]
    return value


# Explicit axes on the model wire avoid Gemini's common row/column convention.
# Canonical application/artifact coordinates remain lists, with no guessed swapping.
Point = Annotated[list[float], BeforeValidator(lambda v: _named_coordinates(v, ("x", "y"))),
    WithJsonSchema({"type":"object", "properties": {
        "x":{"type":"number", "description":"Horizontal position / ORIGINAL PAGE WIDTH, from left (0) to right (1)."},
        "y":{"type":"number", "description":"Vertical position / ORIGINAL PAGE HEIGHT, from top (0) to bottom (1)."}},
        "required":["x","y"], "additionalProperties":False})]
Box = Annotated[list[float], BeforeValidator(lambda v: _named_coordinates(v, ("left", "top", "right", "bottom"))),
    WithJsonSchema({"type":"object", "properties":{
        "left":{"type":"number", "description":"Left edge / original page width."},
        "top":{"type":"number", "description":"Top edge / original page height."},
        "right":{"type":"number", "description":"Right edge / original page width."},
        "bottom":{"type":"number", "description":"Bottom edge / original page height."}},
        "required":["left","top","right","bottom"], "additionalProperties":False})]


class PageRegion(StrictModel):
    page: int
    bbox: Box

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def valid_region(self):
        if self.page < 1 or len(self.bbox) != 4:
            raise ValueError("Source region needs a page and four coordinates")
        l,t,r,b = self.bbox
        if not all(0 <= x <= 1 for x in self.bbox) or l >= r or t >= b:
            raise ValueError("Source region must be normalized with positive area")
        return self


class Measurement(StrictModel):
    label: str
    status: Literal["observed", "unknown"]
    value: float | None
    unit: str | None
    source: PageRegion | None
    note: str

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def grounded_value(self):
        if self.status == "observed" and (self.value is None or not self.unit or self.source is None):
            raise ValueError("Observed measurement needs value, unit and source")
        if self.status == "unknown" and self.value is not None:
            raise ValueError("Unknown measurement cannot assert a value")
        return self
